links.comparator_used: General-purpose 7-8B models (e.g., Qwen2.5-7B) compared with the clinically fine-tuned BioMistral-7B, at FP16 vs INT4 quantization
links.outcome: Accuracy retention on MedMCQA under INT4 quantization (compression robustness)
links.effect: BioMistral-7B (clinically fine-tuned) lost 19.7% on MedMCQA under INT4, more than any general-purpose model
links.tradeoff: Clinical fine-tuning gave no robustness to compression. The abstract also states that safety alignment is determined primarily by instruction tuning rather than clinical domain adaptation.
links.quote: BioMistral-7B, clinically fine-tuned, loses 19.7% on MedMCQA, more than any general-purpose model, showing clinical fine-tuning does not confer compression robustness.

design_hint: quantization precision selection with task-specific validation
